Name: David Moe
Question: Why is our economy in the US and Canada so out of whack that it requires constant intervention by the Central banks like the FED & Bank of Canada? How can any investor have confidence in the future not knowing where interest rates will go long term?
Answer: Central banks are doing a constant balancing act, trying to keep the level of inflation in the currency to a reasonable level, typically between 1 and 2%. This is to promote confidence in the currency. If they didn’t do that, people would start using the currency to wallpaper their house, burn it for heat, or store it in their mattresses rather than banks. The former is hyperinflation, and the latter is deflation. If the central bank properly controls the currency, Investors can calculate their return on investment with reasonable assurance of how much it will be worth. If it doesn’t, investers will shy away from investing their money in the country, and move it to some other country that maintains tighter control over its currency. The US and Canada are popular destinations. As far as interest rates are concerned, investors will lock in a fixed interest rate for a fixed period on contracts with a fixed currency with reasonable expection they will make a profit. They can’t do that in countries which have an irrational government because they never know what their money will be worth.

Name: David Moe
Question: If a Canadian citizen is outside Canada, what would happen if they re-entered Canada irregularly like at the Atlantic shore of Halifax as opposed to an official border entry point?
Answer: There are numerous ports of entry in Halifax, although I have never been there. I just sail the boat up to the dock at the nearest port of entry, tie up the boat and go talk to the customs/immigration officials. The usual questions are name of boat, name of skipper, and number of passengers. Then the passengers have to show their passports to immigration, although where I sailed off the BC coast they didn’t give a damn. One time I pulled up to the dock and the immigration official was walking away with his lunch box because it was almost quitting time. He just pointed at a sign and said, “Call the 800 number” and left. Another time they asked me if I had any liquor on board, and I said yes, but since it was a school trip it was reserved for the skippers and teachers, who definitely needed one. One person I met sailed across the Atlantic to Ireland, tied up the boat, and asked where was the customs officer? They told him he was in the pub, so he found him in the pub. Same questions, name of boat, name of skipper. Then the customs agent bought him a beer and said “Welcome to Ireland”. There are a lot of rules which are widely ignored in the sailing community.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why doesn't the US, Canada, Australia, etc. celebrate Armistice Day?
Answer: The Commonwealth countries celebrate Remembrance Day (also known as Poppy Day due to the tradition of wearing a remembrance poppy) which is a memorial day observed in Commonwealth states since the end of the First World War to honour armed forces members who have died in the line of duty. In most countries, Remembrance Day is observed on 11 November to recall the end of First World War hostilities. The tradition of Remembrance Day evolved out of Armistice Day. During the Second World War, many countries changed the name of the holiday, but not the date. Members of the Commonwealth of Nations adopted Remembrance Day, while the US chose Veterans Day. The common British, Canadian, Australian, and New Zealand Remembrance Day tradition includes a parade with sombre music and one- or two-minute silence to honour the fallen dead. A remembrance poppy is an artificial flower worn to commemorate their military personnel who died in war. The tradition of wearin a poppy to remember the fallen dead arose from a poem by Canadian army physician John McCrae to commemorate the fallen soldiers. In Flanders Fields, the poppies blow Between the crosses, row on row, That mark our place; and in the sky The larks, still bravely singing, fly Scarce heard amid the guns below. The heavy guns would stir up the soil, and the result would be a vast profusion of red poppies on the otherwse destroyed battlefield.

Name: David Moe
Question: Do you also think Canada's oil-rich high Arctic is too valuable to be the privilege of Canada alone? Why not confiscate it and have it managed by a UN commitee to protect the oil fields and garantee constant an oil supply independent from OPEC?
Answer: I worked for a Canadian oil company that ran a drilling fleet of 23 vessels in the Canadian Arctic Ocean. They found more or less no oil at all. It was a complete waste of time and money. The Canadian Arctic is very well drilled up, and it is highly gas prone, with no major oil fields left to find. One of our competitors found exactly one good oil well, and sent in a ship twice a year to take the oil out, but it is now dry and abandoned. There is a lot of oil much further south in Alberta — the third largest oil reserves in the world — but the Alberta govenment has almost complete ownership and control over it. If a UN commitee tried to take control of it, they could expect to be shot in the head at long range with high-powered rifles, it being that kind of place.

Name: David Moe
Question: What is the use of a weak ruble now that Russia no longer needs dollars? Russia needed a weak Ruble before to attract foreign Dollar investment. Now there are no dollars to earn so why does the Russian government still want a weak Ruble?
Answer: On the contrary, Russia is desperately trying to keep the ruble higher than 1 American cent. The ruble has no real value on the international market, so Russians cannot buy anything from another country with it. The Western companies have all pulled out of Russia, taking their dollars and euros with them. Russia’s biggest exports are oil and gas, but the West is boycotting them. China and India continue to buy, but China wants to pay in yuan and India wants to pay in rupees, which does nothing for the value of the ruble.

Name: David Moe
Question: Canada has been more influenced by Germany than Britain due to the high amounts of German immigration (10% of the population is of German heritage). So why didn’t Canada ally with its motherland Germany in WW1/2?
Answer: The Germans who came to Canada were often refugees who didn’t agree with the German government. Others were ethnic Germans who were thrown out of Russia after the Russian revolution, but they didn’t support the German government either. OTOH the British came to Canada for economic opportunities, not because they disliked overcrowded and resource poor Britain. My own ancestors came from Norway to Canada, and after Germany invaded Norway, they volunteered to support Britain. Any time they got a German soldier in their gunsights it was game over. My uncle flew Lancaster bombers everywhere from North Africa to Northern Norway, and his main complaint was that he ran out of Germans to bomb. Other relatives joined the Navy to sink U-boats. The best choice for the Germans was to surrender ASAP because Canadian POW camps were really nice and many of the local girls spoke German.

Name: David Moe
Question: In Canada, the country is an oil exporting nation. With world oil prices plummeting in December 2023 to $70 US per barrel, why are retail prices not declining as well?
Answer: Here in Alberta they are declining. In the rest of Canada you have to deal with your higher taxes and lack of your own oil refineries, because other provinces and the federal Liberal government believe oil is evil and you should be penalized for using it.

Name: David Moe
Question: Isn't Syria the only significant producer of crude oil in the Eastern Mediterranean and possessed of a warm water port?
Answer: No, Syria is a minor oil producer, ranking just ahead of Italy and far behind Algeria and Egypt. The major producers in the area are Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Iran, Kuwait, and the UAE — all of which have huge production and warm water ports, although not on the Mediteranian. They have to ship oil through the Suez Canal or around the tip of Africa to get it to the Mediterranean. Russsia is the world’s second or third largest producer, but it has to ship oil by pipeline or out of the Black Sea into the Mediterranian.

Name: David Moe
Question: Can someone who is living in Canada have a dual citizenship or passport with another country?
Answer: It is quite normal for Canadians to have dual citizenship, and sometimes triple citizenship. My wife, for instance was born in London but the family moved to Canada when she was two. She used to walk around with two passports and go into whichever line was shorter at British airports. Another woman I knew had three passports. She could have had four since she was born in Jamaica, but she had Canada take that information off her Canadian passport since there was no particular advantage to it. Canada will also issue two passports to people from conflict regions — eg. one for Israel and the West, and one for the Islamic countries so they don’t see each other’s visas. During the Iranian revolution they even issued Canadian passports to American diplomats to get them out of Iran. The Iranians thought that was illegal, but the Canadian parliament held a special session to make it legal. Our country, our rules.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why are ‘aboriginals’ exempt from hunting, fishing licenses, and taxes in Canada?
Answer: Why are ‘aboriginals’ exempt from hunting, fishing licenses, and taxes in Canada? It is because their ancestors negotiated treaties with the Crown in which they surrendered most of their land to the white men to farm, log, and build cities, but retained the hunting and fishing rights to the land. They also negotiated freedom from taxes on their reservations, since they had no money to pay taxes. They were not complete fools. When Queen Victoria signed on the dotted line at the bottom, it became Constitutional Law. These treaties cannot be overturned by a majority in Parliament or a Provincial Legislature. Unlike in the US, it requires a Constitutional Amendendment, and that is not going to happen. You wouldn’t believe how many Canadians have some First Nations ancestry.

Name: David Moe
Question: Are Northern American wolves trained to kill Russians? Or do you think the Canadians are trying to create a super pack?
Answer: In my experience, North American wolves tend to stay as far away from human beings as possible. None of them has ever killed a human being. They can be trained, but training a wolf is not easy because they are wild animals. I would put the idea of training wolves to kill Russians into the Absolutely Stupid category. On the other hand, rifles, cannons, and missiles work perfectly well for killing Russians. We have given a lot of them to Ukraine for that purpose.

Name: David Moe
Question: How can a realtor refuse to show my property unless I pay a 3% commission to them if they become the selling broker? My realtor listed my home for 2% total. Can I force them to take 1%?
Answer: Real estate agents have to work to make their money, and the more they make, the harder they work. They save you a lot of time and effort to do the marketing, and they charge accordingly. Where I live the standard commision is 7% on the first $100K and 3% on the rest. You can pay less, but then you get less service. You don’t necessarily have to use a realtor to sell a house. The last house I sold, sold itself. A rumor got loose that I might be thinking about selling it, and a friend of my niece came screetching up, leaving skid marks in the driveway. She looked around and said she couldn’t afford more than $XXX,XXX and since both she and I knew the market price for houses in the neighbourhood, I said that worked for me, and we had a deal. On a previous house I sold, I hired a realtor who lived across the street. She put it on the market, and we sat across the street watching the feeding frenzie and sharing a bottle of wine. We got 4 offers the first day and I just picked the best one. My objective was not to make money (although I got 8 times my purchase price), it was just to have good life and be nice to people. Karma actually works.

Name: David Moe
Question: Upon the changeover from Imperial, Canada hard metricated its milk from one US gallon jugs to 4 litre containers. What did the UK do?
Answer: Canada never adopted the US gallon. It used the British Imperial gallon, which was 4.5 litres versus the American gallon of 3.8 litres. When the conversion from Imperial units to metric units occured, Canada switched to litres, which solved the problem of incompatible Canadian/American standards of measure. US gallons are 20% smaller than UK gallons, so you can’t use them in the UK. Milk normally comes in pints in the UK, but the UK pint is 20% bigger than the US pint. We here in the rest of the Commonwealth just use litres because it is simpler and we are no longer required to use UK or US measurements which differ considerably.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why is Mexico's border with America more difficult to cross than Canada's even though they have the same conditions for visa-free visitors?
Answer: I suppose it is because of the lack of cultural differences between Canada and the US. For instance, consider this cross-border wedding. It was on the Montana/Alberta border. Both families were named Jensen, and they met at the border to unite their respective offspring (cousin marriages are legal in Alberta). After the ceremony, the bride hugged her mother across a farm gate on the border because she had to go away and become a Canadian citizen. One family was from Montana and the other from Alberta. They are united by their common disrespect for their respective federal governments. Note the cattle skull on the fence, something not commonly seen in Eastern weddings in either country. Salaries in Alberta are higher than in Montana, unlike the difference with Mexico, so there is no real incentive for illegal migration to the US. Some people do it accidentally because they get lost and the border is not well marked.

Name: David Moe
Question: Should we rename Canada "North America"? Actually, the US is America itself and Canada is located to the north of America, similar to the way we call all the landmass from Mexico "South America".
Answer: Canada used to be called British North America, but French Canadians didn’t like the word “British” so the Canadian constitution was renamed from the British North America Act to the Canada Act. Canadians in general don’t like to be called Americans and use that word only for residents of the United States of America. They are welcome to it. Mexico is not part of South America. You can consider it to be in North America or in Central America or in Latin America depending on how you divide up the continents. South America begins south of Panama. There are no roads or railroads crossing the Darien Gap between Panama and Columbia which makes it obvious that South America is a different continent.

Name: David Moe
Question: Did you hear on Thursday, November 30/2023 that severe storms that could spawn tornadoes are targeting Texas and Louisiana including the Houston area?
Answer: It sounds like a normal Thursday in Houston. They have depth guages along the roads so people know not to drive into deep water. On a bad day I would see semitrailer trucks floating on their side down the Interstate. If it was a hurricane, my company would shut down all its oil platforms and refineries and send all the workers to Dallas or Baton Rouge. Then, after it was over, they would try to find their missing oil platforms. Restarting the oil refineries could be a challenge, too. One time there was a fishing boat blocking the access road that they had to remove.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why do so many Canadians sound almost Irish but not British?
Answer: I knew an Irish woman who moved from Ireland to Newfoundland to work as a doctor. She couldn’t understand a single word her first patient said. No, it is not the same accent. The Newfoundland accent is an archaic dialect closer to Elizabethan and Shakespearian English than modern English or Irish. Modern English has drifted from its origins so the English no longer pronounce their “r”s. On the other hand, the accent in Nova Scotia (which means New Scotland), is closer to Scottish. There is a strong Scottish influence on Canadian English. The Montreal English accent has strong French influence, although it is peasant French as someone from Paris once told me. He couldn’t even understand their French so he had to speak English. From Toronto on West, the country was settled so fast it didn’t have time to develop an accent of its own, so Toronto and Vancouver English is very similar to Southern California English. I grew up in Central Alberta, and I loved the movie “Fargo” because the actors sounded just like my relatives who lived in Fargo, North Dakota. I can hear the sing-song intonation and odd words they brought over from the Scandinavian countries. Although third generation Canadian, I can speak a little Norwegian myself. However, the school systems Canadianize immigrant children so while they may all look different, they all sound the same — more similar to the standard American accent than most Americans speak.

Name: David Moe
Question: Voters in Europe who cannot stand the refusal of 1-2% of their immigrant population to assimilate vote for far-right parties. How would they feel in San Francisco's Sunset District, which feels like you were transported straight to Guangdong, China?
Answer: If you think San Francisco is very Chinese, you should go to Vancouver BC, which has the third largest Chinatown in North America after New York and San Francisco. It also has the suburb of Richmond (which we call “Lichmond”) which is 3/4 Asian in origin. There are shopping centres there which don’t have any non-Chinese stores. However the Chinese food is fabulous so I always go there. Being Canadian we don’t see any difference between them and us. We are all just trying to live good lives. Canadian schools are very good at Canadianizing their children so after one generation they will all be thinking and talking just like us. And then their children start marrying our children and the population gets totally mixed up. This comes as a shock to their parents. My wife was born in London, England. I had one of her neices here a couple of weeks ago, who was a Malaysian Christian of Chinese ethnicity. She was startled when I told her that one of her aunts was a Jew of Russian origin. The family should talk to each other more, I just listen. Welcome to Canada, we are all the same in our own different ways.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why should women vote when they already have their husband’s vote?
Answer: Because they don’t have their husband’s vote. In the second last provincial election in Alberta, my wife voted for the socialist NDP party, while I voted Conservative. It was her choice. She spent the next four years banging her head against the wall and saying, “How could I have been so stupid!”, but it was her choice. Now she has swung to the right of me, but that is again her choice. She doesn’t have to agree with me. I just have to put up with her ranting and raving about how stupid the Liberals are. I feed a little fuel into the fire from time to time because we are coming to be on the same page — as are most Canadians outside of Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver.

Name: David Moe
Question: Which politicians are the most to blame for Calgary, Alberta's extraordinary urban sprawl? Who approved the development of all those dreadful suburbs?
Answer: It’s not politicians who are responsible, it is homeowners. Calgary is unique in having a very high percentage of home ownership: 72% compared to other cities – Toronto 67%, Vancouver 64%, Montreal 56%, Houston 46%, New York City 35%. Most Calgarians want a house with a front and back yard, not an apartment. It is a democracy and people get what they want. Calgary is also unique in being a unicity — the suburbs are not external suburbs like in other cities, they are part of the city itself. Calgary’s taxes are lower than nearby areas, so Calgarians have an attractive combination of low house prices and low taxes. Condos in the inner city area are more expensive than single family houses in its internal suburbs, so people buy in new communities on the fringes of the city instead. Fortunately Calgary has a very efficient light rail and bus system, so commuting to work is not that difficult. In other cities commuters have an extremely long commute from their far flung neighbouring communities to the inner city, but in Calgary it is not that hard. I would say it is an easy city to raise a family relatively cheaply. In Toronto, Montreal, or Vancouver it has become rather unaffordible. People can move to their far flung external suburb towns, but then commuting times become ridiculous. For all of the above reasons, Calgary is growing extremely fast. So are its surrounding towns, but I can see Calgary annexing them in the future. Calgary is also upzoning the entire city for multi-family dwellings to encourage densification, so you will see it getting denser and denser as the population increases. It is still a very young city. By the end of the century I imagine it will be as big as Toronto is now.

Name: David Moe
Question: Which city has a better economy, Calgary or Toronto? Calgary has a higher GDP per capita, and Toronto has a high GDP. Which is better economically?
Answer: Calgary has higher wages and lower house prices than Toronto, so it is experiencing record levels of in-migration, much of it Torontonians who can no longer afford to live there. In US terms it is like Houston TX versus New York City or Los Angeles. An interesting fact is that Calgary is one of the few Canadian cities where salaries are higher than most US cities. Toronto is a much larger city: it has 6 million people versus 1.5 million in Calgary, but that is not really a good thing — very large cities experience a phenomenon called Diseconomies of Scale, which is to say the bigger they get the more expensive they get. Calgary is more at the sweet spot in city size where salaries have grown but housing prices have not. Both are major head office cities but Toronto is a much bigger if less affordable one. One of my brothers-in-law who lived in Calgary, said they could never pay him enough to move to Toronto. Then he moved to Toronto. I asked what was up, and he said, “I was wrong, they COULD pay me enough”. If you are in the category where companies will shower you with money, Toronto might be OK. If not, Calgary is probably better. My brother-in-law got four university degrees including an MBA and a PhD. Do you fit into the same category? He and my sister later moved to Winnipeg because it was less stressful and big houses in prime communities were dirt cheap.

Name: David Moe
Question: Do bus drivers care if a person hops on and gets off at the next stop (5-10 minute walk away)? Or do bus drivers don’t mind as long as the passenger pays their fare?
Answer: The bus drivers don’t care if you hop on and off as long as you pay the fare. In the nearest major city (Calgary) a transit ticket is valid for 90 minutes from the time of first use. How many times you get on or off the buses or trains doesn’t matter. You can do a tour of the city this way if you buy a daily pass. In the mountain town I currently live in (Canmore) they don’t charge for buses at all, so you can do what you want. They are trying to reduce the amount of car traffic, so buses are free but parking a car costs a lot. The number of parking spaces is limited while the number of tourists is not. We had over 5 million tourists last year, not to mention a few major TV shows being shot to totally screw up traffic. No, that is totally not what it looks like when they are not shooting a movie. Normally we have a bus system called Roam Transit.

Name: David Moe
Question: Can we take science undergraduate program in Canada if we did not take math in 12th?
Answer: If you don’t have grade 12 mathematics, you have approximately zero chance to get into a science undergraduate program in Canada. However you can take high school mathematics in Canada and then apply for university. I would recommend also taking more advanced math (calculus) and if at all possible, be able to solve partial differential equations because it gets really serious really fast in university, in my experience. I didn’t have calculus so I ended up studying 80 hour weeks to catch up. I think it has become more intense since I went to university because Canadians are now the most highly educated people in the world.

Name: David Moe
Question: How much does the spent fuel rod decay after one million years?
Answer: It depends on the isotopes in the fuel rod. There are 5 different isotopes of plutonium. Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241's half-life is 14.4 years. After one million years that fuel rod will probably be about as radioactive as granite rock, which believe it or not, is somewhat radioactive due to the uranium contained in it. Uranium 238 has a half life of 4.5 billion years so your granite fireplace and granite countertops will be somewhat radioactive. They outgas radon gas which has a half life of only 3.8 days. Just make sure your house has good ventilation. There may also be radon gas in your drinking water. If you are really concerned, buy a radon detector — available on Amazon and elsewhere on line. You wouldn’t believe how high the radiation levels in well water can be if it flows through a potential uranium mine. As an aside, the Canadian government did a radiation study on groundwater near a nuclear research facility in the wilderness east of Winnipeg, and as a control also tested the water in wells near the city of Winnipeg. Guess which water was more radioactive? As a solution they just stopped testing the water because it was natural radiation.

Name: David Moe
Question: Is this video proof that the scientific claim that oil is a fossil fuel, is actually a scam ? https://www.instagram.com/p/Cz6a3LXCWJc/?igshid=NTYzOWQzNmJjMA==
Answer: No, it is completely inaccurate. None of it bears scrutiny. Kerosene made from oil was a cheaper substitute for whale oil. Henry Ford discovered that gasoline, which was a waste product often dumped into rivers after the kerosene was extracted, was a cheaper fuel for his cars, which could run on kerosene, gasoline, or alcohol. Other people discovered that kerosene was a cheap heating and lighting fluid compared to whale oil. J.D. Rockefeller just jumped on the train and established an oil monopoly by controlling the railroad system in the US. Calling it a fossil fuel is also misleading since oil forms from marine plankton, tiny boneless creatures which don’t create fossils, only oil. You could call it organic oil instead. That would really infuriate the environmentalists, but having a degree in chemistry I often laugh at a lot of things they say.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why don't gas stations buy future contracts with suppliers to keep the retail price stable?
Answer: Most of them aren’t big enough or have enough financial stability to buy futures contracts. They are just operating on a month-to-month basis. Costco is quite different — it will go out and ask major refineries for a fixed price contract on, for instance, a million gallons of top tier gasoline. It can get get quite a discount on this. All the refineries sharpen their pencils and come in with their best bid. They have of course called the crude oil traders to find out what their best price is. Costco, which is a members-only club, does this to get people to buy memberships and get them into the stores. The similarly low-priced rotissarie chicken (which Costco produces itself) is at the back of the store, so you have to walk past a lot of attractively priced merchandise to get to it. The corner gas station has a similar strategy — they sell gasoline at cost to get you inside to sell you overpriced snacks and groceries. However, they don’t have nearly the market clout that Costco does so they can’t buy top tier gasoline as cheap because they don’t buy it in million gallon quantities. They make most of the money off snacks, soft drinks, and groceries. Their gasoline may be a little bit iffy in quality. Big trucking companies and airlines will also lock in a price, as can municipalities. They can buy it forward for a year or more. One airline even bought its own oil refinery. However Bill & Bob’s Corner Gas can’t do the same. That being said, I have been in Edmonton near Refinery Row, and when they had a surplus of gas, they would sell it off to local gas stations at a deep discount. You just had to drive around and look for it. Edmonton has the lowest prices in Canada because it is surrounded by oil fields and has about 5 big refineries. Alberta also doesn’t have any sales taxes. Canadian leftists in other provinces don’t understand why they have to pay much more. I could write it out in crayon to make it easier for them to understand. On the flip side, I once drove up to a Petro-Canada station near Refinery Row, and it had an “Out of Gas” sign on the pumps. I could see the Petro-Canada refinery from the gas station, and since I couldn’t see 100 foot flames off the flare stacks, I assumed that some refinery in the US had blown up and they were shipping all their gasoline south. Prices go up and down, people there know what is going on, they just have to get used to it. I just drove to the nearby Co-op station. Its big refinery is in Regina and it supplies its own stations first. It is a members-owned cooperative. I’m not really promoting them, I’m just saying they are there (but not in the US) and I have a Co-op membership card. My wife has the Costco card. You just have to learn to play the system. Find out who has the lowest prices this week. It is all supply versus demand.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why aren’t petroleum companies held responsible for capping or compensating all old abandoned oil wells?
Answer: Petroleum companies are held responsible for capping and sealing off old oil wells. There are fines for not properly abandoning old oil wells. Properly abandoning them involves cutting off the steel surface casing 6 or 8 feet below ground level, pouring a concrete plug into the well casing, welding a steel plate over top of it, and then covering it over with dirt. This costs a lot of money — $100,000 per well in my experience, including restoring the surface lease to original condition. If the well is abandoned, you should see nothing but grass on the surface. At the end of it, it should look exactly like it did before the well was drilled, if not better. Some companies would go the full distance and turn them into wildlife refuges c/w picnic tables because it was hard to restore them to the dismal swamps they originally were. They upgraded it from swamp to agricultural land. What you are thinking of is called an orphan well — a well whose owner has gone bankrupt so the company has no money, and the directors and executives cannot be found. It is very hard to extract blood from a stone, as the saying goes. Oil companies do go bankrupt a lot when times turn difficult. Then the government has to step in to properly abandon the well. I worked for an oil company which took over a lot of other companies, and I had a list of 700 orphan wells which we may or may not have owned. If it could be established that we owned them, we would have to go through the abandonment process ourselves or be liable for costs. The mainstream media didn’t understand this at all. The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation had a team of journalists visiting “abandoned” wells in BC. At one they said they just found a metal shack and when they went inside, they found nobody, but the coffee was still warm. At another they found a stack of drill pipe. At a third, all they saw was ponds of water. Unbeknownst to their urban thinking, the first was a field office, the second was a pipe storage yard, and the third was a water injection facility. The oil companies had simply repurposed the well leases for other uses, and the old wells were abandoned, capped, and cut off 8 feet below ground level, or converted into water injection wells. The CBC reporters of course thought it was an environmental travesty, coming from urban centres as they did and not knowing what they were looking at. When they saw a pipe sticking out of the ground, they thought it was an abandoned well, when it was a temporarily suspended well which might be reactivated when oil prices improved. There is a big difference between $10 per barrel oil and $100/bbl oil. We used to hold the leases for 10 years just in case.

Name: David Moe
Question: How long will the US survive if the oil tankers are stopped?
Answer: How long will the US survive if the oil tankers are stopped? Pretty much forever. The US now exports more oil than it imports, and the vast majority of US oil imports come from Canada by pipeline. Canada has the third largest oil reserves in the world. The big Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast refineries would be most affected because they could no longer export oil and products to other countries. California, however, would be completely screwed because it is not connected to the North American pipeline network, which is one reason its fuel prices are the highest of any state. If the tankers stopped sailing, they would all be walking or bicycling to work or shopping. They could all buy electric vehicles, if they could afford them, but then they would overload the electrical grid and burn down the forests.

Name: David Moe
Question: How does the choice of transportation mode impact commuting costs in Canada?
Answer: Walking is the cheapest option. All it costs is the price of new shoes every few years. Bicycling is the second best because eventually the bicycle wears out. Bus or train are third because you have to buy tickets. Cars are dead last because between car payments, repairs, parking, and gasoline, they can exceed your rent or mortgage payments. Myself, I only had a car to go shopping and out into the wilderness on weekends. The rest of the time I used one of the other options — depending on weather. It was the cheapest reliable small car I could buy. And then people wondered how I could afford to have two houses, one in town and the other in the mountains. It was really simple. Don’t commute to work by car and put the money into houses. And on weekend ski trips I felt really bad charging passengers $5 for gas (they insisted on paying) because when I got back to town, the fuel gauge of my little Japanese rice burner was still on full.

Name: David Moe
Question: Could somebody explain the school system in Canada, based on my research on web you supposed to pick 4 primary courses each semester such as math & science but what are that open courses and clubs like art & music and sports, aren't they mandatory?
Answer: Canada has no national school system. Schools are administered by the provincial governments, so there are 10 different systems (13 if you include the northern territories). Quebec is quite different since it is a French speaking province, but the English systems are similar. You start at grade 1 at the approximate age of 6, and graduate from grade 12 a dozen or so years later. In my own province of Alberta, it is an a la carte system. High school has programs and pathways that lead toward university entrance, college and technical schools or directly to work. You pick the path and the school you want. The schools offer a basic diploma, an advanced diploma, the International Baccalaurate (which will get you into any English language university in the world), or French immersion. Pick your goal and the courses you need to get there. Pick the school you want and the courses you want. Competition for the best schools is intense. At a minimum you need to take English, social studies, science, and math. Extracurricular activities are optional. However most students tend to take the maximum they can handle. Alberta has a very competitive job market and the people are very well educated. Canadians in general are the most highly educated people in the world and most people have at least one college degree. That is where you get your real education.

Name: David Moe
Question: How does the cost of living in urban areas like Toronto and Vancouver compare to smaller cities in Canada?
Answer: The smaller cities in Canada are much cheaper than Toronto and Vancouver. The City of Calgary, the closest major city to me and the fourth largest city in Canada, has house prices about half as high as those two bigger cities. Edmonton, the fifth largest city in Canada, has house prices 1/3 of those in Toronto and Vancouver. Calgary and Edmonton are experiencing record levels of in-migration as a result. Smaller prairie cities have even lower prices, but then you have to deal with worse weather. The town of Canmore where I live is rated the least affordable town in Alberta, with average house prices over $1 million. It is also rated one of the most desirable places to live in Canada (comparable to Aspen Colorado or Chamonix France), so retired people from Toronto will sell their house there, come here, and throw $1 million and more down on the table without really thinking about it. From their perspective, it seems reasonable. Usually their kids have gotten jobs working in Calgary and we are only 100 km away. Calgarians come here to walk their dogs, for god’s sake.

Name: David Moe
Question: How does the cost of living in Canada differ for individuals with varying levels of education and professional qualifications?
Answer: The cost of living does not really vary, it is only the income that varies. For instance, one of my cousins was a medical doctor in a small Alberta town. He was not very extravagant, so he only owned a modest house in town and a small cabin on a nearby lake. He also bought six buildings in the downtown core with his leftover money. His accountant suggested he should buy a “quarter” and he thought he meant buying a quarter of beef (1/4 of a cow). No, his accountant meant a quarter square mile of land (160 acres). However, if he lived in Toronto or Vancouver he probably could only afford a small condo. I met a lot of people who started their own oil company, made a fortune, and then didn’t change their lifestyle at all. They lived in the same old neighbourhood with the same neighbours, drove a 6 year old car, and wore cowboy boots and blue jeans to work — A true sign that they owned the company. If there was manure on their cowboy boots, you knew that they really didn’t give a damn about image any more. For professionals with a PhD, they might wear a T-shirt and cargo pants. We used to call the lunch counter at Pay-N-Save Drugs the executive dining lounge because of the millionaires who ate there because it was near the big downtown office towers. They wore old, wrinkled suits. They didn’t get rich by spending money, they got rich by investing it, and the less the spent the more they could invest. Your mileage in the US might differ from our kilometrage here in Western Canada, or even from Eastern Canada where they are more status conscious. In Canada it is important to claim that you are not rich.

Name: David Moe
Question: Should all Canadian conservatives be jailed for voting against our adorable handsome PM Justin Trudeau?
Answer: No, of course not. Canada is a free country and people can vote as they want. Besides, recent poles indicate that 2/3 of Canadians want to vote against Trudeau, and not all of them can be conservatives. There are a lot of liberals and leftists that want to see him gone, too. Adorable and handsome are not good qualifications for PM. Competent and honest are more important, and those are things he is not. His diplomatic performances on the world stage are something of a clown act, and his financial skills are better suited for juggling the books rather than balancing them.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why has Canada's GDP stopped growing in 2023 while America’s GDP is growing by 4.9%?
Answer: Well, as usual on Quora, it is because what you are saying is not true. In logical terms it is called a false premise. The OECD predicts that Canada’s GDP will grow by 1.4% while the USA’s GDP will grow by 1.6% in 2023. Canada’s growth could be higher except for our current anti-business Prime Minister, who hopefully be replaced in the next election. Socialists from Toronto will jump all over that last sentence, but the fact is that most of Canada is not Toronto, and does not like our prevaricating PM.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why is big pharma fighting to keep the price of insulin so high when many people are experiencing this illness and its complications and its cost is less than 5 USD?
Answer: Unknown to many people outside of Canada, insulin was perfected by researchers at the University of Toronto in 1923, including Banting, Best, and their associates. They recieved a Nobel prize for this advance in medicine. To prevent price gouging, they assigned the patent on insulin to the University of Toronto, which then licensed it to companies in Canada and other countries, but insisted they sell it at the lowest practical price. Banting famously declared that “insulin does not belong to me, it belongs to the world”. The price of insulin fell from 1923 to 1942 as manufacturing methods improved. In the US, the medical system is all about making profits rather than benefiting people, which is why medical costs are twice as high in the US than Canada and other developed countries, but the life expectancy is much lower. American pharma companies are patenting minor variations on the original formula for insulin, and selling them for up to ten times as much as the already perfected original formula. The US government, to protect them, prohibits the mass imports of insulin from Canada to the US because that would drive down the prices, and while benefiting diabetics, would cost big pharma their big profits. By 1924 Canadian companies were capable of producing enough insulin to supply the entire world with low cost insulin, and you can imagine how well that would have gone over with American pharmaceutical companies and politicians. Americans should realize that their politicians have sold them a bill of goods about so called “socialized” medicine. Big pharma contributes a lot of big money to American politicians, who not to put a fine point on it, are prone to lying big time. So, Americans do not have universal health insurance like all of the other developed countries, and have to pay much more for their insulin unless they illegally smuggle it across the border from Canada, the original inventor.

Name: David Moe
Question: Are Canadians aware of the fact that their nation used to be much more religious than the United States until the 1960s?
Answer: You are overgeneralizing. While Quebec used to be overwhelmingly Catholic in Canada, the states in the Bible Belt of the US south were somewhat fanatically Protestant. Quebec has somewhat abandoned Catholicism, but the US south remains somewhat fanatically Protestant. My own province of Alberta, which many people assume was like the US South, was settled by a lot of refugees from the US who fled to avoid religious persecution. This included Anabaptist sects like Mennonites and Hutterites, and other non-Protestant groups such as Mormons. Unbeknowst to most people, the largest religious group is Catholics, who have their own government funded religious school system, something which is forbidden in the US but mandatory in Alberta. Now due to record levels of immigration we are having a lot of Muslims and Sikhs coming in — and they get their own publicly funded schools, too. The result is that we do not discuss religion much at family get-togethers. One of my wife’s nieces, who is Chinese Anglican of Malaysian origin, was startled when I told her that one of her Aunts was Jewish. You would think that her husband would have told her, but no. My wife’s best friend is Ukrainian Orthodox, so she got two Christmases — the Anglican Gregorian Christmas and the Ukrainian Orthodox Christmas, since they are on different calendars. She though the Ukrainian Orthodox Christmas was much more fun and had better food than her English Anglican relatives could make. Myself, being of Norwegian Lutheran descent, would have to agree with her. Our traditional Christmas food is an aquired taste, but it takes about 10 years to aquire the taste for it. And those Ukrainian weddings, whoa man! They go on for a week, the food is great (Ukrainian sausage, cabbage rolls and perogies) and the vodka flows freely. OTOH, our family had to impose a “no laughing” rule at Catholic weddings. At Anglican weddings I used to bring my sword to cut the cake, sort of like my Viking ancestors used to bring swords to England.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why didn’t Canadians of German ancestry feel confident enough to stage massive pro-German rallies during WW2 like German-Americans did or to challenge support for Britain? Weren’t they large in numbers like German-Americans were?
Answer: Canadians of German ancestry were overwhelmingly anti-Nazi, which was often why they left Germany in the first place. A large number of them were Germans forced out of Russia after the Russian revolution, and were not really pro-German, but definitely anti-Russian. They were sympathetic to German POWs who arrived in Canada during the war and even gave them jobs working on their farms while their daughters liked to charm the German soldiers, leading to a lot of mariages. After the war was over, most of the POWs applied for Canadian immigration. German immigrants were somewhat surprised at how friendly Canadians were in general. But the fact is that the German-Canadians were on a completely different page from the Nazis in Germany. They wouldn’t hesitate for a second to shoot a German Nazi dead, but if the German soldier offered to surrender, they would accept that surrender, speaking German and feeling sorry for him. Otherwise, otherwise.

Name: David Moe
Question: How is it that I want to build a nice house first than get married?
Answer: In my experience, if you build a nice house in a nice neighborhood, you can barely fight the women off with a stick. Once they find out, they want to move in with you, marriage totally optional. You have to be careful, though, because many of them are totally crazy. It is important to get them on the right meds. In my own case, after dating approximately 100 women (I’m not bragging, I’m complaining) and even marrying one who divorced me, I found my perfect match. I can remember the look of shock and awe on her face when I accidentally proposed to her while driving down the highway on the way back home from a vacation. After 17 years of marriage, she is now looking after me in my old age, and will get the house when I am gone, which the town on its tax notice claims is worth over $1 million — about 10x what it cost to buy the land and build on it. And I built it with my own two hands. (although It took four strong men to lift the big ceiling beams into place.)

Name: David Moe
Question: Do you think Calgary is doing enough when it comes to sustainability?
Answer: Calgary has one of the largest light rail transit systems in North America, one of the largest bicycle path systems in North America, and some of the largest urban parks in the world. Despite being the oil company head office centre of Canada, its people are not environmentally insensitive. A lot of other cities, not to mention the federal government, only give lip service to sustainability. Calgary does something about it. Oil is something they sell to other people who don’t have any oil.

Name: David Moe
Question: Is Canada losing its argument as a better country to live in than the USA?
Answer: No, I think that Canada is proving it is a much better country to live in than the USA, notably 3 major cities rated among the top 10 most livable in the world. Canada has universal health care, longer life expectancy, lower infant mortality, a much better educational system, and lower murder rate than the US. The USA is kind of descending into third world status on all those indicators, and has a real dumpster fire of a political system with a government shutdown looming and an ex-president who has been impeached twice, found to be guilty of civil fraud, and who has four criminal trials to face in the coming months. So, while Canada is far from perfect, it is not nearly that bad. We can only complain about having an ineffectual prime minister who does more or less nothing.

Name: David Moe
Question: Do any of the Walmarts in Ottawa Ontario Canada sell Heinz pure white vinegar as I checked 3 locations so far and none of them had it?
Answer: White vinegar is white vinegar no matter whose label is on the bottle. It is 95 percent water and 5 percent acetic acid. It is equally as useful for cleaning out bathroom sink drains and killing toe fungus as for cooking, and not very expensive. Why would you insist on Heinz white vinegar from Walmart when it is all the same and available at every supermarket and grocery store?

Name: David Moe
Question: If chicken/beef is dried in a food dehydrator like for jerky, just meat and salt added, how long, if at all, could it be left at room temperature in a sealed bag/container?
Answer: In my experience, it lasts more or less forever. If you put beef in a dehydrator for about half a day, it removes all the moisture, which prevents bacteria from growing in it. Then if you use a vacuum sealer to remove all the air from the plastic bag before sealing it, the lack of air also prevents bacteria from growing. I used to walk around with beef jerky in my backpack for years before eating it. It was a great source of emergency calories and protein, as well as being a nice snack on the trail. You don’t want to run out of food on a long backpack because you will start stumbling and falling down, which many people didn’t seem to realize. Chocolate bars will keep you going for an hour or two, beef jerky will keep you going for half a day. Pemmican can keep you going for months, but that is a more serious survival food used by fur traders who paddled half way across the continent on 50 pound bags of it. It was 50% bison meat and 50% fat, and never rotted.

Name: David Moe
Question: Do you ever wonder if "organic" and "all-natural" labels are just fancy marketing tactics to make us pay more for the same product?
Answer: It is all marketing. For instance Earthbound Farms sold fresh organic salad (picked by Mexicans from laser-leveled fields), but got an offer to sell salad to Walmart. Walmart didn’t want to sell “organic” salad, so they took the “organic” label off it and sold it cheaper. Same salad, lower price. However, if they put the “organic” label on it, they can make more money. “Organic” according to my university chemical textbooks, means “of or pertaining to an organism”. I once worked for an oil company that grew fungus on a crude oil base and sold it as an “organic” product, which is technically correct since crude oil is organic in nature. People who don’t have chemistry degrees and never worked for an oil company read a lot more into it.

Name: David Moe
Question: I'm a 33 yr old woman. Is it too late to find a partner who will love me and want to marry me?
Answer: It’s never too late. My mother was 35 when she married my father, and she was 37 when I was born, the first of four kids. She would have had more but her biological clock ran out. She used to almost break her arm patting herself on the back for what great kids she had raised. In my case, I accidentally proposed to my wife when she was about 48 and I was 54. Driving down the highway after a kayaking trip which had gone extremely well, I said something like “Maybe we should consider formalizing our relationship”. Her jaw dropped, her eyes opened, and she said, “Was that a marriage proposal?!!” And I kind of had to sort of admit that it really was. We were married a few months later. We have been married for 17 years now. She has worked out better than my ex-wife (she calls herself the “Trophy Wife”) and previous 100 girlfriends (That’s an estimate — I’m not bragging, I’m complaining). You just have to meet the right person. Sometimes if you are a woman you have to kiss a lot of toads before you kiss the frog that turns into your handsome prince.

Name: David Moe
Question: Does 4 quarts equal up to 3 liters for making coolaid?
Answer: It depends on whether you are using American quarts or British quarts. 4 American quarts are 3.8 litres, 4 British quarts are 4.2 litres. That is why we Canadians always measure volumes in litres because they are always the same. Note British and not American spelling for litres.

Name: David Moe
Question: I have read that the average Canadian accent in Ontario now sounds like a coastal California accent, so much so that people who live in Ontario sound like they come from the San Francisco Bay Area or Greater Los Angeles. Is this true?
Answer: Canada has one of the largest dialect continuums in the world. It extends from Ontario across all the Western provinces to BC, where all the people speak more or less the same. It occurred because the region was settled so fast in the late 19th century, and there was no time for regional dialects to emerge. The Canadian Pacific Railway line was built in about 4 years, so people jumped on the train and went west to homestead the land in large hordes. Many of them didn’t speak English, so their kids learned textbook English in school and all spoke the same. Similarily, there is a dialect continuum across the western US that extends south from Seattle to San Diego. It also evolved fast as hordes of immigrants moved west. People in San Diego speak more or less the same as people from Seattle, and people from Seattle don’t speak much differently from people from Vancouver, Canada (there is also a Vancouver, Washington but we’ll skip over that little detail of shared history.) In addition, a million or so Canadians moved to California to take advantage of the warmer weather. The result is that the Los Angeles accent is not much different than the Toronto accent. Canadian actors only have to remember the pronunciation of about 3 words to get it right in Hollywood movies. And trust me, there are an awful lot of Canadian actors down there, and a lot of Hollywood companies shooting movies in Canada. Just follow the script and remember that Zed is pronounce Zee in the US. Caveat — a linguistics expert can probably determine where they came from within 100 miles by listening to them talk, but most people are not linguistics experts.

Name: David Moe
Question: Can a Catholic woman and a half-Muslim half-Catholic man get married?
Answer: Of course they can. They can go Las Vegas, get a couple of witnesses off the street, and be married by an Elvis impersonator. They can go to the Caribean and be married by the captain of a boat. There are honeymoon packages which include this, which are very popular. Where I live, couples can fly to the top of a mountain with as many guests as the helicopter can carry, and be married by a mountain guide. More commonly, in this area, there a lot of large marriages on old coal mining sites, which have been reclaimed by the community to look very, very nice, with a spectacular view of the mountains. You can get a licence from the Alberta Motor Association, and find some kind of clergy person or someone else authorised by the provincial government to perform marriages, invite a few friends, or a hundred, and just do it. The government doesn’t care about religions and doesn’t ask what they are. One of my wife’s nieces who is Malaysian and Christian, but of Chinese ethnicity, who was staying with me last week was startled when I told her that one of her aunts was Jewish of Russian origin. But people don’t advertise that kind of thing, they just are what they are. I told her that I was nominally Lutheran but was leaning more toward Confucianism in my beliefs, which confused her even more. I call Canadians “Heinz 57s” from Heinz’s 57 varieties of pickles.

Name: David Moe
Question: Are Canadians in favour of Justin Trudeau?
Answer: According to recent polls, only 26% of Canadians want to have Trudeau as Prime Minister any more, and over half of them want an election this year. He is only protected from defeat by the leftist NDP and only because they would lose most of their members if they triggered an election by a vote of No Confidence at this time. This is unlike the US because a vote of No Confidence in Parliament at any time forces the PM and his cabinet to resign, and triggers a national election to replace them and all the Members of Parliament. There is no such thing as Impeachment in Canada. Governments simply get fired and voters decide who will replace them. Regionally, the Conservatives are well ahead in Western Canada, including BC, and the NDP is second in the West. The Conservatives now lead ahead of the Liberals in Atlantic Canada. In Quebec, the Block Quebecois is ahead and the Liberals are running third. It is not a good time for the Liberal Party in Canada. Trudeau is clearly past his best-before date as PM because most Canadians are tired of him.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why did Justin Trudeau say that the carbon tax/rebate system would cost nothing to Canadians? And if that is true, why did he just cut the carbon tax for Atlantic Canadians?

Atlantic Canadians were becoming very upset at the increase in their home heating costs due to the increasing price of fuel oil, which is mostly used in the Atlantic provinces. He has 24 MPs whose seats are at stake in Atlantic Canada, versus 2 MPs in Alberta which produces most of Canada’s natural gas, but has more people than all 4 Atlantic provinces combined. Name: David Moe
Question: What is known about the introduction of horses into the First Nations of the B.C., Canada interior? Horse culture was in place in the interior dry belt at the time of European contact in Canada in the early 1800’s.
Answer: From archeological studies and Native history, it is know that the Spanish brought horses to Mexico after their conquest of the Americas. Some of them got loose or were stolen, and fell into Native hands. Native peoples found it was much easier to ride than walk, so they spread the animals through the North American West by the first half of the 1600s—long before they encountered Europeans. Researchers compared the ancient horses’ DNA with that of modern horses and found that the centuries-old equines had largely Spanish ancestry. Archeologists’ findings suggest horses spread from Spanish settlements in the American Southwest (formerly Mexico) to the central Great Plains and northern Rockies by the first half of the 17th century because that was an ideal ecosystem for horses. No doubt Native peoples, who were not hindered by national boundaries, rode them up into the interior of BC, where they thrived under the semi-arid conditions, with lots of dry grass to eat. Horses were extremely useful to Native people who used them to hunt and to pull their teepees and goods on travois, hence their rapid spread. Previously they had to use dogs to pull their travois, which they referred to as their “dog days” when they were much less mobile. People don’t realize this and associate Native people with horses, which had actually arrived in the West a century or two before Europeans and were not native to the Americas. They had become extinct in the Americas several millenia before.

Name: David Moe
Question: Can my landlord evict me for not paying late fees?
Answer: In Alberta, where I live, provincial law prohibits late fees or penalties to be charged or enforced for late payment or non-payment of rent. OTOH, what will happen is that the landlord can give you a 14 day pay or quit notice. If you don’t pay within 14 days, you can be evicted. The sheriff’s deputies will come, remove you and your possessions to the curb, and the landlord will change the locks. If you try to go in without a key, you will be charged with breaking and entering, which is a crime. This is more abrupt than some other jurisdictions, but mild compared to Texas, where you will get a 3 day pay or quit notice. Not paying the rent on time is a fundament breach of the lease agreement. On the other hand, rents in these places are much lower than other jurisdictions.

Name: David Moe
Question: Have you noticed that the leaves on many trees in Canada aren’t changing colour this year, and that they are just turning sad brown and falling off instead?
Answer: No, where I live in the Canadian Rocky Mountains we had a truly spectacular fall. The park authorities had to put in parking restrictions in the parks to handle the crowds who went out to watch the alpine larches turn colour. The Siberian larch I planted in my front lawn did its own spectacular colour show, and the ubiquitous aspen also were beautiful. The griffin poplar my neighbour across the street in his back yard has gotten to be huge, about 3 times the height of his house, and also put on its own colour show. Unfortunately it is over now, all the leaves have dropped, and now we have to deal with shoveling snow. Where is this global warming they promised us? From Wikipedia ©2005 Walter Siegmund under the terms of the GNU Free Documentation License, I don’t know where you live, but if you have a depressing fall, maybe you should move to somewhere more exciting.

Name: David Moe
Question: How does Justin Trudeau decide which Canadians should pay the carbon tax and which ones are exempt?
Answer: I think his standard is that Canadians who don’t vote Liberal have to pay the carbon tax, and those that do vote Liberal will be exempt. A Trudeau minister admitted Saskatchewan families are being punished with the carbon tax because they don’t vote Liberal. The Saskatchewan government has responded by refusing to collect it for them. This causes a constitional crisis. Trudeau won the last election with the smallest margin in Canadian history, and the Conservatives actually got more votes than the Liberals. He promised electoral reform in his first election, but realized that under a reformed electoral system he would have lost, so that promise was quickly and quietly shelved. Trudeau lost most of rural Canada and Prairie cities, and only got elected on the basis of votes from Atlantic Canada and the largest urban centres of Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver. He is suffering from an excess of arrogance, and is likely to get his party wiped out in the next election if he keeps doing this kind of thing. He is running far behind in the polls.

Name: David Moe
Question: Why has the government of Saskatchewan unanimously voted to stop remitting carbon tax payments to the Government of Canada?
Answer: It is because the Trudeau Liberal government, in an attempt to preserve the 24 seats it is at risk of losing in Atlantic Canada, has decided to suspend its carbon tax on home heating oil in the four Atlantic provinces, while preserving it in the other provinces. Saskatchewan does not vote Liberal for obvious reasons like this, so it is not going to cooperate with the federal Liberal government to collect the tax. This means the federal government is going to have to collect the carbon tax by itself, which is going to make the Liberals even more unpopular in Saskatchewan, not that they can get any members elected there anyway. Saskatchewan mostly uses natural gas for home heating which has half the carbon footprint of heating oil, but is not exempt from the tax. It is mostly the Atlantic provinces which use heating oil made from imported oil since they are not on the national oil and gas pipeline system. The rest of the country uses cheaper Canadian oil and natural gas, and resource rich Canada exports much more oil to the US than it uses itself. It is only the Atlantic provinces which are trapped into using more expensive OPEC oil. Justin Trudeau is following in the footsteps of his father and previous Prime Minister, Pierre Trudeau, in getting the Liberals wiped out in Western Canada. This kind of selective taxation goes over very badly in the rest of Canada, particularly since the Liberals will have to increase taxes dramatically to pay for their reckless spending during Justin’s reign, incurring a rather large national debt. It took decades for subsequent governments to pay off the debts his father incurred. And here we are again.

Name: David Moe
Question: What accounts do Native Americans today have of the unprecedented and absolute devastation of their populations due to diseases?
Answer: They have no records at all because Native Americans didn’t have writing, and their oral histories don’t talk about it, if it actually happened in reality. As a result, activists can just make things up. You can hypothesise that such a decline in population happened, but you can’t know for sure without objective evidence. The only evidence is remains of abandoned villages and territories, but the white men arrived in their territories generations if not centuries later, when it was all over. The diseases were brought in by the Spanish but spread on their own much faster than white settlement. That was at a time when contageous diseases could wipe out half of the population of a continent, which happened in Europe when the Black Death arrived. Smallpox could also wipe out a third of the population in Europe, and the Europeans were used to having a third of their population killed by contageous diseases. It probably killed a higher proportion of Native Americans due to their lack of herd immunity caused by centuries of people dying, but nobody really knows. At that point in time, half the children in London didn’t live to reach adulthood, which tells you how bad it was. Daniel Defoe’s “Journal of the Plague Year”, although mostly fictional, gives you a feel for what it was like. When the death rate in London from bubonic plague dropped from 80% to only 30%, people went out to the pubs to celebrate. And unfortunately the antivaxxers are convinced that is the vaccines and antibiotics that will kill you, and not these nasty fatal diseases.

Name: David Moe
Question: What do career politicians do when they get voted out of office in terms of living income assuming they have no fall back savings? Do they start hunting for regular jobs?
Answer: In Canada, Conservative leaders can make far more money in the private sector than they can in government. After they leave politics, they can become consultants and be paid large amounts of money for just giving advice to companies. Stephen Harper, who was Prime Minister from 2006 to 2015 is probably making hundreds of thousands of dollars as a consultant, far more than he could make in government. If someone is appointed to the board of directors of a major company, they can make a lot of money for just showing up for occasional meetings and giving their opinion — because they know how the government works — and if they are on the board of a dozen or so companies at $50,000 or so per directorship, the numbers really add up. By contrast, politicians for the socialist New Democratic Party don’t really have any future except working for the government in some left-leaning province. Private companies don’t want them. One of the problems the Canadian Conservative party has is that their members get elected to Parliament at a very young age, before they have any real job experience. For instance, the current leader of the Federal Conservative Party, Pierre Poilievre, started campaigning at the age of 16 and after getting his BA was elected to Parliament at 25, making him one of the youngest MP’s in history. He became a cabinet minister at the age of 34. He became leader of the Conservative Opposition at the age of 43. If he becomes PM (which seems likely at this point in time), after he leaves office he will have a very lucrative retirement as a consultant. This contrasts with the rather geriatric leaderships in American politics where nobody seems to be less than 70 years old and many of them are pushing 80.

Name: David Moe
Question: Would you say that Justin Trudeau's new policy on carbon tax is a compromise or a double standard?
Answer: It is obviously a double standard because only the provinces in Atlantic Canada are eligible for the carbon tax exemption on heating oil, but BC is not. Trudeau has 24 members in Atlantic Canada he wants to get re-elected, and the people there use heating oil, whereas other provinces seldom do so. Heating oil on the East Coast is already very expensive because it is imported from foreign countries, whereas the rest of the country is on the Canadian pipeline system and has cheaper oil and gas. Heating oil is also twice as carbon-intensive as natural gas, and infinitely more than hydro-electric or nuclear power. I have been warning Canadians for quite some time not to use oil for heating because the price depends on global conditions. A war on some other continent can cause the price to skyrocket, e.g. the Russo-Ukrainian war. There is natural gas offshore of Nova Scotia and Newfoundland, so why don’t they use it? Instead, Nova Scotia sends its natural gas to New York and burns oil imported from other countries to heat peoples houses at a higher cost than their own offshore Sable Island gas. How rational is that? It wouldn’t work except for federal subsidies. The federal Liberals want to build offshore wind farms instead, at vastly greater cost, with a time frame of decades.

Name: David Moe
Question: My landlord sold the house I live in. What time do I have to leave? Do I get money to move?
Answer: There is a lot of confusion about this. Under Common Law, a lease is attached to and runs with the property, not the owner. Your lease is an asset that was sold with the house. If the new owner wants to get you out, he/she has to give you proper notice, which under common law is 30 days on a month-to-month lease. Where I live (Alberta) it is 90 days on a month-to-month lease. Alberta is somewhat tenant friendly. On a longer lease, the lease expires on the original end date, but the landlord must give you 30 days notice that they are not going to renew it, otherwise it reverts to a month-to-month lease and the 30 or 90 day rule applies. Read your local landlord and tenant act to see what applies. Also read your lease to see what it says, but remember, the lease cannot override the landlord/tenant law. No, you do not get money to move. In my experience you find a friend with a pickup truck and get a few other friends to help. If you don’t have any friends, hire a moving company.

Question: Why is the fat of fish more healthy than other sources?

There are also omega-6 and omega-9 fats, but omega-9 fatty acids aren’t strictly “essential,” as the body can produce them. You can actually die from lack of fat — it is called protein poisoning, which occurs when the body takes in too much protein without enough fats and carbohydrates for a long period of time. Other names for this are “rabbit starvation” or “mal de caribou.” because neither rabbits nor caribou have much fat in their bodies. Early explorers died from it after a long period of living solely on rabbits or caribou. Fish, on the other hand, have adequate amounts of omega-3 fats in their bodies, as well as a number of other essential nutrients that human beings need to survive. Some of my Norwegian ancestors lived for 90 or 100 years on a diet consisting mostly of fish. They also grew very tall because of the amount of high quality protein in the fish.

Question: My great grandma still talks about the "Great Depression" and she's almost 100. Was it actually that bad or is she just being dramatic?

The girls had to make dresses out of flour sacks because they couldn’t afford store-bought ones. There was also a major drought and the topsoil in many areas dried up and blew away. The advantage they had in Alberta where I lived was that it was a major agricultural area. Farmers could only get $5 for a cow, so rather than sell them, they ate them themselves or gave the meat to relatives, friends, and complete strangers. They ate well but their diet was limited to what they could grow (no fruit and limited vegetables) and they were not well dressed. Electricity and running water were luxuries that many people couldn’t afford. When WW2 came along, things got a lot better. The men volunteered for the armed forces where at least they got paid, and when they came back from the war there were jobs aplenty. There were also some extremely frustrated women waiting for them who really, really wanted to get married, hence the post-war baby boom, and a man could support a wife and four children on his wages alone back then.

Question: What influenced Vancouver's decision to use light rail trains (avg. 25-40 km/h) instead of the heavy rail favoured in Toronto and other metros with trains moving around 50-80 km/h?

There is also a concept called light metro which is entirely grade separated, but uses LRVs in moderately longer trains using automatic train control. Few medium sized cities can justify the cost of a heavy rail system since they don’t have enough passengers. A two-track LRT system has the passenger capacity of a 16 lane freeway if you build it for that, and it takes a lot of cars off the road. It saves the cost of building a bigger freeway since the cost of an LRT track is about the same as a freeway lane if you avoid gold-plating it like Vancouver did with its Skytrain. Question: If a large gold deposit was found on government land, could the government mine it or would the government be required to sell the land before it could be mined?
Answer: The government would lease the mineral rights to land to a mining company since the government is not in the business of mining gold. The mining company would pay a royalty to the government based on the value of the gold mined. The terms of royalty payments would be laid out in a licensing agreement. The mining company only owns the gold rights to the property, and some other company could log trees or graze cattle on the same land if it got a lease for the lumber or grazing rights. I worked in the Land Department of an oil company, and we used to say you could slice land more ways than balogna. We would lease the mineral rights for oil and gas from the government, and the surface rights to drill a well from some farmer. We only needed 4 acres for a well site and lease road. They couldn’t deny us a lease because we owned the mineral rights. Some farmers who had a grazing leases from the government thought they could stop us, but the judges ruled that grazing cattle was not incompatible with drilling oil wells, and we had the right to drill a well to produce our oil. Our problems arose with farmers started grazing their cattle on our well site surface leases, and driving their trucks on our lease roads. There was also a problem with farmers storing hazardous chemicals on oil well sites, because the chemicals they used were far more more toxic than the chemicals oil companies used, and we were under much more government supervision. The title to my house says, “… excepting thereout all mines and minerals …” which means I only own the surface rights, which allowed me to build a house on it. The house sits on an enormous coal deposit, but I don’t own the rights to the coal. It doesn’t really matter because the town is not likely to allow a mining company to undermine my house because it has had streets fall into mine tunnels and had to be repaired at millions in costs. On the other hand, an oil and gas company could run a horizontal well a mile below my house, and I could do nothing about it because it would affect nothing on the surface.

The other 3 colonies declined to participate, but became 5 colonies because of the massive influx of refugees from the United States (the United Empire Loyalists). Originally, Canada was a French province, but after the British conquest it became a British province. It declined to participate in the American revolution because it had nothing in common with the American states. Because of the huge influx of American refugees after the American War of Independence, it was split into two halves: Lower Canada (now Quebec) which was mostly French and Upper Canada (now Ontario) which was mostly English. This created a lot of English/French conflicts, so in 1867 Upper Canada (Ontario) and Lower Canada (Quebec) combined with Nova Scotia and New Brunswick to create the Dominion of Canada with 4 provinces. Since then it has expanded to 10 provinces and 3 northern territories.

Question: Is $130K/year enough to support a family of four comfortably in downtown Calgary, Alberta if my spouse doesn't work?

If you don’t mind a commute, there are new suburbs popping up around Calgary like fairy ring mushrooms in your lawn. It is one of the fastest growing cities in North America.

Question: Does Canada have administrative divisions below provincial city and sub-provincial municipalities?
Answer: The Canadian constitution covers two levels of government: federal and provincial. Any level below that is organized by the provincial governments. Local governments are sometimes called “creatures of the province” because the provincial governments can insert more levels of government or remove local governments at will. For example, the Ontario provincial government once created another level of government above the City of Toronto called Metro Toronto, which included the city and its suburbs. Then when they decided that wasn’t working, they abolished Metro Toronto and annexed the suburbs to the centre city. Toronto has been reorganized several times by the Ontario government, sometimes without consulting the City Council or its residents. On the other hand, my own province of Alberta dissolved several underpopulated counties and turned them into Improvement Districts, which are governed directly by the provincial government. For that matter the City of Fort McMurray, which has 73,000 people, abolished itself and amalgamated with Improvement District No. 143 to create the Regional Municipality (RM) of Wood Buffalo. They did this for tax reasons — Wood Buffalo has the giant Athabasca oil sands plants within its taxation area, but has no cities or towns. Fort McMurray is a Specialized Municipality with no city government. Alberta has numerous different types of municipal organization, and it has always felt free to reorganize them whenever it wanted to.

Buy warm clothing. Calgary is better as regards climate and there are more office jobs, but you might need a master’s degree to have a good chance of getting a job. Alternatively there is waiting tables and flipping burgers.
